tool_args.rationale: The open-branch measurements shift sharply with s_grad and match the verified two-layer siphon's gradient-inhibited saturating flux plus signed square-root branch term. Numerically fitting its three target parameters to all seven paid rows is preferable to another probe; no high-frequency chaotic signature is present.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The existing seven measurements show a strong direct dependence on sink gradient, while all have the same horizon and do not establish temporal dynamics; the lower-complexity static siphon mechanism directly explains the observed branch shifts.
The largest observed gradient is 2.3, below the archive's stated trigger range (>2.36), so an avalanche-specific probe is not currently indicated.

considered_alternatives.option: Quartic radiation or smooth polynomial response
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The opposing shifts at different s_grad for similar u_now conflict with a gradient-independent quartic law; the verified siphon note specifically predicts gradient inhibition and an open-branch term.
It is explicitly a nuisance measurement and does not resolve the remaining uncertainty in the mechanism.
